caption_en:
Why is it called the WEST Bank? 🧭 Because there's an EAST Bank.

1922: the League of Nations' Mandate for Palestine covers both banks of the Jordan.
1921: on the East Bank, Britain had already made Abdullah, a Hashemite prince from Mecca, Emir of Transjordan: about 77% of the Mandate's area.
Sept 1922: the League's Transjordan memorandum: the Jewish national home clauses don't apply east of the river.
1948: Abdullah's Arab Legion takes the land west of the river.
1950: Jordan annexes it (only Britain and Pakistan recognised it): "the West Bank", as opposed to the East Bank. Its Palestinians become Jordanian citizens.
1967: Israel takes it. 1988: Jordan drops its claim.
Today an estimated 55 to 70% of Jordanians have Palestinian roots (estimates vary). Queen Rania's parents are from Tulkarm and Nablus.

King Abdullah II (2014): "Jordan is Jordan and Palestine is Palestine." Palestinians seek their own state in the West Bank and Gaza.

Two banks. One river. One people?

Send this to someone who says "West Bank".
caption_he: למה "הגדה המערבית"? כי יש גדה מזרחית. המנדט על פלשתינה (1922) כלל את שתי גדות הירדן, וכ־77% ממנו הפכו לעבר הירדן של האמיר עבדאללה. ב־1950 ירדן סיפחה את הצד המערבי וקראה לו "הגדה המערבית". היום, לפי הערכות, 55 עד 70% מהירדנים ממוצא פלסטיני. שתי גדות. נהר אחד. עם אחד?
